slides.0.title: Industry and market
slides.0.subtitle: Cooperatives, volume IGPs, exports and spirits markets
slides.1.title: The power of cooperatives
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Plaimont
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Decanter: about 800 members and 5,300 ha; it produces 98% of Saint-Mont AOP, over half of Madiran and Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh and almost half of Côtes de Gascogne IGP (an older figure)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Everyday volume
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The same piece: the entry-level white Colombelle L'Original reaches about five million bottles a year
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Background
slides.1.highlights.2.content: When André Dubosc arrived in 1973, production was declining because demand for the white base wine used for Armagnac had collapsed (Decanter)
slides.1.content: Cooperatives kept varieties and volume alive in remote areas.
slides.2.title: Côtes de Gascogne: export volume
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Export orientation
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Wikipedia: production potential above 100 million bottles with 75% exported; Wine Folly also says about 75% of its wines are exported
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Scale and extension
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Nearly 12,000 ha in the Gers, about two-thirds of the area; the total reached 15,000 ha after the 2005 extension (Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: White share differs
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Wikipedia gives Gers output as 91% white, 8% red and 1% rosé, while Wine With Seth says about 85% is white; the share is not tested
slides.2.content: This is the varietal, export-volume model.
slides.3.title: Armagnac and exports
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Main markets
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Drinks International (2021): the US is Armagnac's second-biggest export market behind China, with China first by volume
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Tariff impact
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The US imposed a 25% tariff on certain European spirits, turning a €100 cellar price into €125; BNIA data: exports to the US fell 11% in 2020 and those to China almost 31%
slides.3.content: These are 2020–2021 conditions and do not describe the present.
slides.4.title: Other market angles
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Cahors exports
slides.4.highlights.0.content: About 25% is exported and exports doubled between 2004 and 2013 (Wine With Seth); the Argentina Malbec partnership began in 2007
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Price range
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Madiran runs from about €10 for cooperative wines to over €100 for prestige single-vineyard cuvées (Wine With Seth)
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Remoteness
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Decanter's Jefford notes that Plaimont's area lies at least two hours from Bordeaux or Toulouse, a disadvantage turned into an advantage
slides.4.content: The South-West is positioned on value and distinctiveness, not scale.
